channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: Wily coyote who swam to Alcatraz gets ‘much fatter’ on prison island diet
item.description: Officials are monitoring if the canine is preying on the island’s seabirds.

item.title: The end of Allbirds? Tech’s favorite shoe company will close nearly all locations
item.description: Workers cleared out the chain’s Hayes Valley location Tuesday, one year after the Jackson Square flagship shuttered.

item.title: Silicon Valley reacts — kinda, sorta — to the violence in Minneapolis
item.description: Things are different than in 2020. But workers at tech companies are starting to ask for some action.

item.title: Junk science about Levi’s Stadium substation becomes a problem 49ers can’t ignore
item.description: GM John Lynch said the “health and safety of our players is of the utmost priority.” Now the team must show its work.

item.title: AI is booming. Tech jobs in San Francisco are not
item.description: The city lost thousands of jobs last year as layoffs at major companies outpaced hiring.

item.title: Fry up the plátanos: The Bad Bunny Bowl is officially a food holiday
item.description: The superstar is known for supporting his people through his stomach. Bay Area Puerto Rican restaurants are heating up the fryers.

item.title: Kawakami: Here’s the Warriors’ long-shot path to winning the Giannis sweepstakes
item.description: Golden State has long believed that if the nine-time All-Star had his druthers, Steph Curry’s presence would put this franchise on the short list of destinations.

item.title: SF prices out of this world? Try a starter home on planet Mandar
item.description: A new exhibit at Madrone Art Bar features an interactive, intergalactic AI real estate agent selling $3 billion penthouses on alien moons.

item.title: The 18 best events in SF this weekend
item.description: A “Heated Rivalry” party, Black History Month celebrations, the 25th Edwardian Ball, a dog adoption event, and more.

item.title: Is the Shvo over at the Transamerica Pyramid?
item.description: The developer’s German investors are experiencing buyer’s remorse after pouring retirement savings into remaking the San Francisco icon.
